end.name: Abu Madi gas field / gas treatment plant (Ḩaql Ghāz Abū Māḑī), Dakahlia Governorate
end.coord_source: GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Ḩaql Ghāz Abū Māḑī' (a named oilfield/gasfield feature, GeoNames ID 7780529, located via geonames.org/search.html); corroborated within ~1.3 km by an unnamed OSM industrial-landuse way (690414942/690415406) footprint in the same location

corridor_note: Both endpoints pin to named, independently gazetteered locations ~43 km apart on a near-straight bearing across flat Nile Delta terrain, consistent with a short trunk feeder rather than a winding local network line.
length_check: Great-circle distance Damietta<->Abu Madi field = 43.1 km vs sheet LengthKnownKm=42.00 km (ratio 1.03) — excellent agreement; corridor is essentially the straight-line chord.
notes: Sheet's Start governorate cell is blank and End=Dakahlia; both are consistent with the resolved endpoints (Damietta city sits in its own Damietta Governorate, Abu Madi field sits in Dakahlia) so no governorate mismatch here. GEM's own internal country-note materials (read only as a research lead, never cited) had previously flagged an unnamed OSM industrial way ~1.3 km from this GeoNames point; I independently re-ran the Overpass query myself and confirmed that same unnamed industrial feature exists at this location, rather than taking the country note's claim on faith. No name was found for that OSM way, so it corroborates PRESENCE of industrial infrastructure at the site, not the 'Abu Madi' name itself.

start.name: Al-Ma'addiyyah / Boughaz El-Maadia channel (Lake Idku outlet to the Mediterranean/Abu Qir Bay), near Idku, Beheira Governorate
start.coord_source: OpenStreetMap node 768567336 ('قلعة المعدية' / Al Muaddiyah fort, at the Idku outlet channel); the channel's identity and function ('Al-Madiyyah Channel, connecting [Lake Idku] with the Mediterranean') independently confirmed in Wikipedia's 'Idku' article, which does not itself give a precise point coordinate

end.name: Damanhur (city), Beheira Governorate capital
end.coord_source: Wikipedia infobox coordinates for Damanhur, corroborated by GeoNames gazetteer entry for Damanhur (within ~200 m)

corridor_note: Straight-line chord (38.6 km) undershoots the sheet's 50.0 km, but the corridor must in reality skirt Lake Idku and Abu Qir Bay wetlands rather than cross them, so a longer real path than the chord is expected and does not contradict the endpoints.
length_check: Great-circle distance Meadia<->Damanhur = 38.6 km vs sheet LengthKnownKm=50.00 km (ratio 0.77) — plausible for a route that must detour around Lake Idku.
notes: GOVERNORATE MISMATCH TO FLAG: the sheet's Start governorate for P8077 is 'Damietta', but the resolved Meadia/Al-Ma'addiyyah endpoint sits at the Idku outlet channel, which is in BEHEIRA Governorate, not Damietta — as is the End endpoint (Damanhur, also Beheira). I have not altered the sheet value; this is reported for a reviewer to adjudicate, not silently corrected, per the task's instruction. 'Meadia' in the GEM pipeline name is a transliteration of 'Al-Ma'addiyyah' / colloquial 'Maadia', the name of the channel/strait connecting Lake Idku to the sea near Abu Qir Bay -- not a governorate or a large town in its own right, which likely explains why the sheet's governorate column for this end may have been populated incorrectly (possibly confused with Damietta, another Delta port city with a superficially similar administrative role). Only one precise-coordinate source (the OSM node) was found for the exact anchor point; the Wikipedia corroboration confirms the channel's name/function/general area but not a specific lon/lat, so confidence is capped at medium rather than high.

start.name: Alexandria (city/metropolitan area) — NOT resolved to a specific named facility
start.coord_source: Averaged/approximate: Wikipedia infobox coordinates for Alexandria city center (31.19750, 29.89250) and GeoNames gazetteer entry for Alexandria as first-order administrative seat (31.201762, 29.91582); these two independent public sources disagree by ~2 km on 'Alexandria's' point location, which is itself evidence that no single fixed point is the right answer here

end.name: Damanhur (city), Beheira Governorate capital
end.coord_source: Wikipedia infobox coordinates for Damanhur, corroborated by GeoNames gazetteer entry for Damanhur (within ~200 m)

corridor_note: 'Alexandria Network' is the name used in an independent, real-world source (see notes) for GASCO's Alexandria-area gas distribution grid as a WHOLE, not one facility -- so unlike P8076/P8077/P8075, there is no single named take-off point to anchor. I could not identify a specific city-gate/compressor/distribution station carrying this exact name with the remaining research budget (WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task; only WebFetch on pre-identified URLs remained available). The length check below is itself informative: it argues AGAINST an Alexandria-city-center start point.
length_check: Great-circle distance from Alexandria city-center coordinates to Damanhur is 55.8-57.8 km (using GeoNames vs Wikipedia city-center points respectively) -- LONGER than the sheet's stated 45.00 km pipeline length, which is geometrically impossible for a real route (a real corridor is always >= the chord, never <). This means the true 'Alexandria Network' take-off point is NOT the Alexandria city center; it must be a point measurably closer to Damanhur, plausibly somewhere along the Alexandria-Cairo desert/agricultural corridor (e.g., in the vicinity of Kafr El Dawwar, an industrial town roughly midway between Alexandria and Damanhur) -- but I was not able to independently source-confirm this as the actual 'Alexandria Network' takeoff point, so I am NOT reporting Kafr El Dawwar as a finding, only flagging it as an unconfirmed hypothesis a reviewer with more search budget should test.
notes: UNRESOLVED START ENDPOINT. The pipeline name and the Wood Mackenzie-sourced Egypt Oil & Gas feature article (egyptoil-gas.com) both independently confirm 'Alexandria Network-Damanhur' as a real, named pipeline in Egypt's gas grid (alongside 'Meadia-Damanhur', 'Abu Madi-Damietta', etc., all in the same source list) -- so this is NOT a fabricated or GEM-only name, but the source describes the pipeline taxonomy, not a specific facility location for the Alexandria end. Recommend a follow-up pass (fresh WebSearch budget) searching GASCO/EGAS Arabic-language sources for 'شبكة الاسكندرية' city-gate or take-off station once the session's search quota resets. Sheet governorate columns (Alexandria -> Beheira) are plausible on their face and not flagged as an error, since 'Alexandria Network' by definition originates somewhere in Alexandria Governorate; the open question is WHICH point within it.

end.coord_source: OpenStreetMap way 352865112, explicitly tagged name='MIDOR', industrial=refinery, operator=EGPC; corroborated by MIDOR's own official site confirming its address as 'Amreya Free Zone, Alexandria Egypt'

corridor_note: P8075 shares its exact PipelineName ('Western Desert Gas Complex-Ameriya Gas Pipeline') and Start/End province pair (Western Desert -> Alexandria) with sibling rows P8065 ('Pipeline I', 15.00 km) and P8066 ('Pipeline 2', 14.50 km), which already carry applied 'very low (straight line/schematic)' routes anchored to this same WDGC-area/MIDOR pair (10.2 km apart per that prior work). I independently re-derived and re-verified that same anchor pair from public sources rather than taking the prior routing on faith (see refs above) and it holds up: the two ends I found sit essentially the reported 10.2 km apart (10.43 km by my own calculation).
length_check: Great-circle distance WDGC-cluster<->MIDOR = 10.4 km vs sheet LengthKnownKm=26.00 km (ratio 0.40). This is markedly lower than siblings P8065/P8066 (~0.68-0.70 by the prior work's reasoning), meaning 'Pipeline 3' is asserted to be notably less direct than 'Pipeline I'/'Pipeline 2' between the same two points, or possibly serves a slightly different pair of facilities within the same dense industrial zone that I could not distinguish from these two anchors alone. I am reporting the same family-consistent anchor pair as the two siblings (per the task's request to fix endpoints for route creation), but flagging the ratio gap for a reviewer's awareness -- it is a corridor-shape question, not a name/identity question.
notes: 'Western Desert' in this pipeline's Start-governorate column is a GEM label shared identically by P8065/P8066/P8075 and by the much longer (~230 km) Obaiyed-Amreya trunk family (P0474/P6687/P3934); for the short (14.5-26 km) 'Pipeline I/2/3' rows the true endpoints sit entirely within Alexandria's Amreya industrial zone, not in the literal Western Desert (Matrouh) -- this label mismatch is inherited/pre-existing across the whole three-row family, already implicitly accepted in prior GEM route work on P8065/P8066, so I am noting it for completeness but not raising it as a new finding specific to P8075.
